title: docmeta persona vocabulary (1.0.0-proposal.1)
description: The contract for a document that *defines* a persona — the reader a page means when it says `personas: [persona-platform-admin]`. This is the other end of that reference, and the place docmeta:audience:1.0.0-proposal.1 deliberately sent reader level when it cut `expertise` from the page: level is a fact about the persona, so it lives on the persona. The document's name and summary stay `title`/`description` (docmeta:core:1.0.0-proposal.1), its parent segment is `audiences` and the journeys it takes are `journeys` (docmeta:audience:1.0.0-proposal.1), and its upkeep is docmeta:stewardship:1.0.0-proposal.1's — a persona is a page like any other, and inherits the family it sits in. Wired with an `overrides:` glob over the directory personas live in; there is deliberately no `type: persona` constant, because `type` is the registry's most contested key and pinning it would trade stackability for a claim the config already makes.

id.description: The stable anchor pages point at — `persona-enterprise-docs-lead`. Required, where core leaves it optional, because every `personas:` value in the corpus resolves here; the whole value of the reference is that it does not dangle.

role.description: What this person does, in their own org's words — `Manager/Director of Documentation`, `SRE on call for the platform`. The one required fact beyond identity, because a persona without a role is a label: it names a group without saying who is in it, and every downstream judgment — which content types serve them, what they already know — hangs off the role. Deliberately not enumerated and deliberately singular: it is prose about one person-shaped reader, not a taxonomy.

expertise.description: What this reader already brings — `docs-as-code`, `git-and-prs`, `kubernetes-operations`. **This is where reader level lives**, and the reason docmeta:audience:1.0.0-proposal.1 has no `expertise` field: a page claiming `expertise: beginner` beside `personas: [persona-expert-admin]` could contradict the persona it points at, so the fact sits at the altitude that owns it. Baseline knowledge and prerequisites are one list on purpose — a separate `prerequisites` key would both duplicate this at a slightly different confidence and collide with docmeta:structure:1.0.0-proposal.1's `prerequisites`, which means the opposite thing (what a *page* needs, not what a *reader* has).

goals.description: What this reader is trying to accomplish, one line each — `keep a multi-product corpus current without new headcount`. The persona-level counterpart of a page's `intent` (docmeta:audience:1.0.0-proposal.1): `intent` is the job one page serves, these are the jobs the person has. Free text, because a goal that fits an enum was never a goal.

pains.description: What blocks them today, one line each — `cannot see what changed across many repos`. Kept beside `goals` rather than folded into it because they are what the docs must actually answer, and because a persona document with goals and no pains is usually a persona nobody interviewed.

needs.description: What this reader most needs documented, as labels — `security-and-self-host`, `roi-reporting`. The same key and shape as the audience vocabulary's, deliberately: the two never judge the same document, because each is wired to its own directory, so one coverage report can read the segment's needs and its personas' needs through a single column. Where `goals` and `pains` are prose for a human, this is labels for a query.

evidence.description: What this persona was derived from — `customer-interviews`, `support-tickets`, `user-testing`. The difference between a researched reader and an invented one, recorded where a reviewer can see it. Recommendations, not a closed list.

evidence-strength.description: How far the evidence goes: `strong`, `moderate`, `thin`, `assumed`. Enumerated because a strategy-coverage report switches on it; absence means unassessed, not strong. Same ladder as the audience and journey vocabularies, so the report is one query.

stringList.description: One non-empty string, or a non-empty list of unique ones. The empty list is rejected on purpose: `goals: []` reads to every downstream consumer as goals recorded, and it is the opposite.

evidenceSource.description: One evidence source: a recommended value, or any non-empty string. The enum branch is advisory; the open branch keeps an org-specific research channel a correct document rather than a violation.

evidenceList.description: One evidence source, or a non-empty list of unique ones — the same one-or-list shape as stringList beside it and as kg's labelList, so a value ports between altitudes unchanged. The empty list is rejected on purpose: evidence: [] reads as evidence recorded, and it is the opposite of that.
